mainTopic: A son comes before a daughter in inheritance, even from relatives, and judging inheritance cases is a court matter done only by day
overview: The גמרא asks what new law comes from the statement that daughters inherit from their mother's brother. רב ששת answers that it teaches the order: sons come before daughters. A ברייתא uses the word ״וְיָרַשׁ״ to compare inheriting from relatives to inheriting from a parent, so in both cases a son comes first. Then רבה בר חנינא teaches from ״בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ״ that inheritances are divided by day and not at night. אביי objects that someone who dies at night obviously still leaves an inheritance. So he suggests the rule is about a בית דין judging inheritance cases, since the whole section is called ״חֻקַּת מִשְׁפָּט״. He supports this with רב יהודה: three people visiting a חולה may write his instructions or act as a court, but two may only write. רב חסדא adds that acting as a court works only by day, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does the earlier statement come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law comes out of the statement it just mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law was this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the earlier statement was needed, since it seems obvious. This question sets up רב ששת's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement says that daughters inherit from their mother's brother. That seems obvious, because their mother would inherit from him and they inherit from her. So the גמרא wants to know what new law the statement adds.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What practical difference does this make?

phrases.english: For what law [was this said]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a statement made before this section begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law the statement about daughters inheriting from their mother's brother teaches.

steps.title: Sons come first
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the statement teaches that sons come before daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: To teach who comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains that the point of the statement is the order of inheritance: sons come before daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement does not just tell us that daughters can inherit, which is obvious. It tells us that when there are both sons and daughters, the sons inherit first, even when inheriting from a relative such as an uncle.

keyTerms.meaning: To come first, to take priority
An אמורא who answers the question

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: To precede.
phrases.notes: He means that when there are sons, they come before the daughters.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The statement teaches the order of inheritance: sons come before daughters.

steps.title: A son comes before a daughter even when inheriting from relatives
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא compares ירושה from relatives to ירושה from a parent. In both, a son comes before a daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק taught before רב הונא: The word ״and he shall inherit״ compares a secondary inheritance to a primary inheritance. Just as in a primary inheritance a son comes before a daughter, so too in a secondary inheritance a son comes before a daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives a source in the פסוק showing that a son comes before a daughter even when the inheritance comes from a relative, not a parent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child inheriting from a parent is called the 'primary' inheritance. Inheriting from other relatives is called the 'secondary' inheritance. The word ״וְיָרַשׁ״ links the two, so the rule that a son comes first in the primary case also applies in the secondary case. This matches רב ששת's idea that sons come first.

keyTerms.meaning: Primary inheritance: a child inheriting from a parent
Secondary inheritance: inheriting from other relatives
A son comes before a daughter

steps.whatToRemember: Because of the word ״וְיָרַשׁ״, a son comes before a daughter both when inheriting from a parent and when inheriting from other relatives.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak taught before Rav Huna:
"And he shall inherit" –
it compares the second inheritance to the first inheritance;

phrases.aramaic: מָה יְרוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה – בֵּן קוֹדֵם לַבַּת,
phrases.english: just as with the first inheritance, a son comes before a daughter,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יְרוּשָּׁה שְׁנִיָּה – בֵּן קוֹדֵם לַבַּת.
phrases.english: so too with the second inheritance, a son comes before a daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source in the פסוק that fits רב ששת's rule that sons come first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In inheritance from relatives, just as from parents, a son comes before a daughter.

steps.title: Inheritances are divided only by day
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חנינא teaches that the words ״on the day״ mean inheritances are divided by day and not at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חנינא taught before רב נחמן: ״And it shall be on the day that he causes his sons to inherit״ teaches that by day you divide inheritances, and you do not divide inheritances at night.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A ברייתא learns from the word ״בְּיוֹם״ (on the day) that dividing inheritances happens only in the daytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have simply said 'when he causes his sons to inherit.' Since it says ״בְּיוֹם״, the ברייתא reads that word as a limit: daytime yes, nighttime no. At this point the ברייתא does not yet say exactly what kind of 'dividing' it means. That will be the question in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר חֲנִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Chanina taught before Rav Nachman:
"And it shall be on the day that he causes his sons to inherit" –
by day you distribute inheritances,
and you do not distribute inheritances at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר חֲנִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the time of day when inheritance is handled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inheritances are divided by day and not at night.

steps.title: אביי objects: people who die at night still leave an inheritance
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that a simple reading of the ברייתא leads to an impossible result.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, only someone who dies by day is inherited by his sons, but someone who dies at night is not inherited by his sons?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the ברייתא. If inheritance only 'happens' by day, then a person who dies at night would leave nothing to his children, which is obviously wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי understands 'dividing inheritances' as the inheritance itself passing to the heirs. But a person becomes an heir automatically at the moment of death, whatever the time. So this reading cannot be right, and the ברייתא must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, then according to what you say

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. He is showing that one way of reading it fails, and in the next step he offers a better reading.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But if so,

phrases.aramaic: דְּשָׁכֵיב בִּימָמָא הוּא דְּיָרְתִי לֵיהּ בְּנֵיהּ,
phrases.english: [only] one who dies by day is the one whose sons inherit him,

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּשָׁכֵיב בְּלֵילְיָא לָא יָרְתִי לֵיהּ בְּנֵיהּ?!
phrases.english: [while] one who dies at night, his sons do not inherit him?!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר חנינא's ברייתא that inheritances are divided only by day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read simply, the ruling means that someone who dies at night leaves no inheritance. That is absurd, since heirs inherit no matter when the death happens.

steps.title: אביי's better reading: deciding inheritance cases in court
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that the ברייתא is talking about a בית דין judging inheritance cases, which happens only by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you were speaking about the judging of inheritances?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a new reading of the ברייתא. The day-only rule is about a court deciding inheritance cases, not about the inheritance itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heirs own the inheritance right away, day or night. What must happen by day is the court case: a בית דין judges only in daytime. Reading it this way removes the problem raised in step 5.

phrases.english: Perhaps you were saying [this about] the judgment of inheritances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 5 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to mean that inheritance itself passes to the heirs only by day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means that a court judges inheritance cases only by day.

steps.title: Proof: the whole inheritance section is a matter of judgment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the inheritance section is called ״a statute of judgment,״ so it follows court rules, including judging by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: ״And it shall be for the children of Israel a statute of judgment״ teaches that the whole section was set down to be a matter of judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי supports his new reading with a ברייתא. Inheritance is called ״מִשְׁפָּט״ (judgment), so inheritance cases are court cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק at the end of the inheritance section calls it ״חֻקַּת מִשְׁפָּט״. The ברייתא learns from this that the whole section counts as a court matter. Court matters are judged by day, which explains why רבה בר חנינא's ברייתא said inheritances are handled by day.

keyTerms.meaning: A statute of judgment, a law handled by a court

steps.whatToRemember: Inheritance passes to the heirs at death, no matter the time. But judging an inheritance case is a court matter, and the court does it only by day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that a בית דין deciding inheritance cases follows normal court procedure, such as sitting only in daytime.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "And it shall be for the children of Israel a statute of judgment" –

phrases.aramaic: אוֹרְעָה כָּל הַפָּרָשָׁה כּוּלָּהּ לִהְיוֹת דִּין.
phrases.english: the entire section was placed to be [a matter of] judgment.
phrases.notes: He means the whole inheritance section is treated as a court case and follows court rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's reading that the day-only rule is about judging inheritance cases.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on במדבר 27:11, ״לְחֻקַּת מִשְׁפָּט״, showing that the inheritance section is a court matter.

steps.title: Three visitors to a sick person can act as a court
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports his reading with רב יהודה. Three people visiting a חולה may write his instructions as witnesses or act as a בית דין. Two may only write.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this matches רב יהודה, who said: if three people came in to visit a sick person, they may choose to write his instructions, or they may choose to act as a בית דין. If there are only two, they may write, but they may not act as a בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings רב יהודה's ruling to show that handling a sick person's property for his heirs can be done as a real בית דין action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three people make a בית דין, so they can either sign as עדים on a document or rule as a court. Two people are only witnesses, so they can write but cannot judge. This shows that dividing property for heirs can be a court action, which fits אביי's answer that ירושה cases are judged by a בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: They write the instructions down and sign as witnesses
They act as a court and make a ruling
Three people, the number needed for a בית דין

steps.confusionAlert: Writing and judging are two different things. Writing makes them witnesses on a document. Judging makes them a court, and that needs three.

phrases.english: And this is like רב יהודה,
phrases.notes: אביי is still talking here. He backs up his idea that ירושה cases are handled by a court.

phrases.english: as רב יהודה said:
Three people who came in
to visit the sick person,
if they want, they may write,
phrases.notes: They write down how the sick man wants his property given out, and they sign as witnesses.

phrases.english: if they want, they may act as a court.
Two people may write
but they may not act as a court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule from an אמורא to the ברייתא proof that ירושה follows court rules.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that dividing a ירושה can be done as a בית דין action
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's ruling about three visitors to a חולה acting as a court
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three visitors may write or judge. Two may only write.

steps.title: This was taught only by day
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits רב יהודה's ruling: the three visitors can act as a court only by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: this was taught only when it happened by day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a limit to רב יהודה's rule. The visitors can act as a בית דין only during the day. This sets up the next line, which explains what happens at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court does not judge at night. So the choice to act as a בית דין works only by day. This matches רבה בר חנינא's teaching that inheritances are divided by day and not at night.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in a certain case
An אמורא who adds a limit to רב יהודה's rule

steps.whyThisMatters: It brings the סוגיא back to its main point: ירושה, as a court matter, is handled by day only.

phrases.english: And רב חסדא said:
They taught this only by day;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב יהודה's rule to the daytime.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three visitors can act as a court only by day.
